From: Sophie Lin <sophie@driftwave.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Partial availability on 2026-10-12 — request for credit and timeline reconciliation

Hi Roahn,

We saw a sustained partial degradation on our synthetic probes against your /v1/generate endpoint on 2026-10-12 between ~09:06 and 09:28 PDT (customer side timestamps). Our monitoring recorded high error rates and token-level timeouts that impacted several of our downstream services.

We checked public status and noticed a maintenance window you published that day starting at 09:09 PDT. However, our probe logs show failures as early as 09:05. We're concerned this is a clock skew / time-sync mismatch between our probes and your maintenance metadata — that skew would change whether the downtime is considered within your maintenance exclusion period.

Can you:
- Confirm the authoritative maintenance window start time and timezone for the 2026-10-12 event.
- Share the Redwood ingress/egress logs for the region serving us for that timeframe.
- Confirm if any third-party CDN or peering change was active during that slot (we saw a CDN routing spike in our network trace).

We've attached our probe log export for the timeframe (CSV). We appreciate a resolution/update since this incident intersects our renewal review.

Thanks,
Sophie Lin
Head of Edge Reliability
DriftWave Media

Attachment: driftwave_probe_logs_20261012.csv (CSV, 128KB)

- Check whether a third-party CDN handoff or peering change was in effect (we saw a peering reroute notification but not at the same timestamp).
- Provisionally hold this for the SLA review board — if we confirm maintenance fully covers the window we will exclude it; if not, we'll calculate an apportionment.

Hi Sophie, Roahn — looping in myself to clarify our apportionment approach so expectations are clear.

Notes on methodology (short):
- Redwood's uptime ledger uses ingress acceptance timestamps (our gateway logs) in UTC and applies maintenance exclusions based on the published window in UTC.
- Where a customer's probe timestamps predate our acceptance timestamps, we perform a clock-skew analysis; if skew > 30s we treat probe timestamps as potentially inaccurate for exclusion decisions.
- If a third-party (CDN/peering) routing change is shown to have contributed, we consider a split credit approach: partial customer credit + third-party attribution.

Given the facts you provided:
- Your US probes appear NTP-synced (±2s) — good.
- Our preliminary logs show maintenance metadata start at 2026-10-12T16:11:00Z (09:11 PDT). That is ~2–6 minutes after your earliest samples, depending on which probe farm you reference.

Proposal: provisional credit of 50% of the impacted window while we complete a forensic correlation (we'll export token-level accept/reject events and gateway CPU scheduling traces). If our forensics show the majority of the errors align to a CDN handoff at 16:11Z independent of our scheduled maintenance, we will reclassify and adjust accordingly.

Sophie — can you confirm if the traceroute snapshots map to our listed egress ASN (we'll provide the ASN list in the ledger export)? Also please confirm you agree to the provisional split so we can apply a one-time account credit while final reconciliation completes.

Thanks,
Ben Carter

Hi Sophie — thanks for the fast turnaround and for confirming your US probes were NTP-synced. We've completed the ledger export and correlated token accept timestamps to your epoch samples. Summary below and next steps:

What we found:
- Redwood maintenance metadata (published) shows the maintenance event window started at 2026-10-12T16:11:00Z (09:11 PDT).
- Our gateway logs record the first notable token rejections at 16:05:40Z, but the volume of rejected tokens materially increases beginning 16:11:03Z.
- Traceroute evidence indicates a CDN handoff at ~16:11Z that coincides with the jump in error rates. The early samples (16:05–16:10Z) are low-volume and match early probe retries from one of your edge farms.

Decision and credits:
- Given the mixed signal (small number of early errors prior to maintenance + large-scale impact coincident with maintenance/CDN handoff), we've issued a provisional account credit equal to 50% of the billed units for the impacted minute range. This aligns with Ben's proposal. The credit will appear on your next invoice; reference: SUP-3421.
- We will continue correlation work with the CDN provider and will adjust if further evidence clearly attributes the window to third-party routing. If so, we'll re-open and apportion accordingly.

Attachments included: redwood_maintenance_schedule_20261012.ics, uptime_ledger_export_20261012.csv (token-level events).

Next steps:
- Marissa's SRE team will share a short technical post-mortem to Sophie (expected EOD 2026-10-20).
- If DriftWave wants a joint call with the CDN provider for cross-correlation, we'll coordinate dates.

Sophie — thanks again for the thorough logs; that sped this up. If the credit amount or classification is material for your renewal conversation we can escalate to a credit committee review.

Best regards,
Roahn Mehta
Product Ops — Redwood Inference
